true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write

The code decrypts `user.backupCodes`, nulls the matched entry in memory and writes the whole re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both read the array before either writes, so the same single-use code is accepted twice. Likewise, two concurrent logins using two different codes will each write back their own copy of the array, and the last write resurrects the code consumed by the other request. Consuming the code should be done atomically (e.g. inside a transaction with a conditional update / row lock) so a code can be redeemed exactly once.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code branch allows login without password verification

In `authorize()` the password is only verified when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` at line 121). The new backup-code branch at line 131 is evaluated for `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` regardless of whether a password was checked, and it takes precedence over the TOTP branch. A request that sends any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") together with a valid `backupCode` therefore skips password verification entirely and also never validates the TOTP code, so the backup code alone grants a session. Backup codes are meant to be a second factor (they are even downloaded to a plain text file / copied to the clipboard), so this turns a leaked backup code into a full account takeover. The backup-code path should require successful password verification before accepting the code.

Unvalidated backupCode body field can crash the endpoint

`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string. A client sending a non-string JSON value (number, array, object) makes the handler throw a TypeError, which surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error. The same pattern exists for `credentials.backupCode` in next-auth-options.ts. The field should be validated (type and expected format) before use. Also note `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is unguarded and will throw a 500 if the stored value cannot be decrypted/parsed.

"missing_backup_codes" message points to a settings flow that does not exist

The new string `missing_backup_codes` says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." but there is no UI anywhere in this PR to generate or regenerate backup codes: codes are only created inside `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup`, which rejects users who already have 2FA enabled (`TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`). Every user who enabled 2FA before this change (and any user who closed the dialog without saving the codes) will hit this error and will be told to do something that is impossible without first disabling 2FA. Either add a regeneration endpoint/UI or change the message to tell the user to disable and re-enable 2FA.

Assertion on the 2FA switch is a no-op and is left unfixed

`expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the unawaited Promise returned by `isChecked()`, which is always truthy, so the first test never verifies that 2FA was actually enabled (the PR adds a FIXME acknowledging this instead of fixing it). With the new backup-codes step inserted into the flow this assertion is the only post-enable check in that test, so a regression in the enable flow would not be caught. Use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or the `[data-state="checked"]` locator as the second test does.

No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code

The core new behaviour of this PR — authenticating with a backup code in `next-auth-options.ts` (including single-use consumption) and in the disable endpoint — has no automated coverage; the added test only clicks the download/copy/close buttons on the new dialog and the file notes this as a TODO. Regressions such as a code being reusable, or the "Lost access" flow sending the wrong field, would go undetected.

Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar (now a common case: handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one). The very next line dereferences it unconditionally: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and aborts `EventManager.create()` for any Google Meet booking made by a user without a destination calendar. Use optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: destructuring evt.destinationCalendar when it is null or empty leaves mainHostDestinationCalendar undefined, and the subsequent unconditional access to .integration throws a TypeError. The candidate focuses on the create path and proposes optional chaining, but it is the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
createEvent ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId

`selectedCalendar` is now resolved only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` explicitly handles that case by calling `createEvent(credential, event)` without an externalId. For those rows the `find` returns `undefined` and the event is created in `"primary"` instead of the user's configured destination calendar — a regression from the previous `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. A fallback to the destination calendar matching this integration (or the first one) is needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug in destination calendar selection: the lookup logic fails to correctly resolve the configured destination calendar, causing events to be created in the wrong calendar. The golden comment describes a self-matching externalId comparison, while the candidate describes a credentialId-only lookup that misses nullable credentialId rows and regresses from externalId-based selection. These are the same underlying calendar-resolution logic error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug assignment logic inverted

`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the previous condition `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The intent is: when billing is enabled the slug is only *requested* (stored in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment), otherwise the slug is set directly. With this change, a billing-enabled instance sets both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug`, and a non-billing instance (self-hosted) creates the organization with **no slug at all**, so org subdomain resolution/`orgDomains` lookups break for newly created orgs. This change is also unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same logic inversion: the slug conditional was flipped relative to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED, so billing-enabled orgs set both slug and requestedSlug while non-billing orgs set neither.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Calendar.createEvent credentialId made a required parameter

`createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` adds a required second parameter to the public `Calendar` interface. Any caller outside of `CalendarManager` (other packages/apps, third-party calendar app implementations in the app store that are invoked directly) that calls `createEvent(evt)` now fails type-checking, and at runtime receives `undefined` for `credentialId` — which in GoogleCalendarService makes the destination-calendar lookup fail and silently writes to `primary`. Making the parameter optional and defensively handling `undefined` would avoid both the contract break and the silent misrouting.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same breaking change: Calendar.createEvent now requires a credentialId parameter, violating the existing interface contract for callers/implementations that still use the single-argument signature. The candidate emphasizes external callers and runtime undefined behavior, while the golden emphasizes unupdated implementations, but the underlying contract break is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Video booking references no longer store credentialId

`credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for non-calendar (video) results; the previous code used `result.credentialId` in that branch. Video meeting references are therefore persisted with `credentialId: null`. Cancellation logic depends on it: `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy (see packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts ~line 491), so Zoom/MS Teams/etc. meetings will silently stop being deleted when a booking is cancelled.

updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId

`externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` are read from the results of `updateAllCalendarEvents`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-323) does not return `externalId` or `credentialId` at all — only `createEvent` was changed to return them. Previously these values came from `evt.destinationCalendar`. As a result, every booking reference created by an "edit location" action loses its calendar linkage, and subsequent updates/cancellations can no longer resolve the right credential/calendar (they fall back to iterating all credentials or to "primary").

updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match

`event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the ternary's else branch), so it compares each `cal.externalId` against `undefined`/`""` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Consequently, when no external calendar id is passed, `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined })` is issued instead of targeting the destination calendar, and the update fails. The intent was presumably to fall back to the first (main host) destination calendar.

Hangout-link patch sends calendarId: undefined

In `createEvent`, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` uses `selectedCalendar` directly, but `selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined` (the `|| "primary"` default was moved to the insert call only). When the destination calendar can't be resolved, the insert succeeds against `primary` while the patch that adds the Meet link to the description is sent with no calendarId and fails.

Duplicate calendar events created for multiple destination calendars without credentialId

For each destination with no `credentialId`, the code filters *all* of the organizer's credentials of that integration type and creates an event with each. With the new multi-destination array (e.g. two collective hosts both having a Google destination calendar with `credentialId: null`), this loop runs once per destination using the same credential set, producing N duplicate events in the same calendar. The per-destination branch should create at most one event for the destination it is iterating over.

updateAllCalendarEvents error message computed but never logged

The catch block still builds the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed in this change. Calendar update failures are now swallowed entirely with no log output, making production debugging of failed reschedules/updates impossible.

Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none

`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining, and `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case all the collected host destination calendars are discarded, so collective hosts get no calendar invite — exactly the scenario this PR aims to fix. Initialize the array (e.g. `[]`) before pushing, or build the array in one expression.

Dynamic-booking user select no longer fetches organization slug

The rewritten `loadUsers` dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the `prisma.user.findMany` select used for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings. This field was added deliberately for org-aware booker URLs; without it any downstream use of `user.organization?.slug` resolves to undefined (or fails type-checking because the two branches of `loadUsers` now return different shapes), producing wrong links for dynamic group bookings in organizations. The removal is unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor.

Empty dynamicUserList surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400

`throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is a plain `Error`, so the catch below (which only re-wraps `HttpError` and Prisma errors as 400) converts it into `HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. A malformed/empty client-supplied user list is a client error and previously did not produce a 5xx; this will pollute error monitoring and give the booker no useful message.

Recurring-cancellation deletion repeated once per calendar reference

The recurring + `allRemainingBookings` block (which itself loops over every user calendar credential and every updated booking) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With multiple calendar references (the normal case for the new multi-host destination calendars) the same delete calls are issued refs × credentials × bookings times, multiplying external API calls against Google/Office and relying on 404/410 swallowing for correctness. The recurring branch should run once, outside the per-reference loop.

Webhook payload destinationCalendar shape is now inconsistent (null vs []) and breaking for consumers

`destinationCalendar` in the webhook payload changes from an object/null to an array, but the code paths are inconsistent: BOOKING_REJECTED/confirm now emits `[]` (this assertion), while BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still assert `null` (lines 119 and 373) because handleNewBooking sets `null` when there is no destination calendar. External webhook consumers parsing `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break, and they now have to handle three shapes (object-less array, empty array, null). The shape should be normalized (always an array) and the payload change documented as breaking.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in its `calendar` field (silent contract change + floating promise)

`getCalendarCredentials` stays synchronous but `getCalendar(credential)` is now async, so each returned item's `calendar` property is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of a `Calendar | null`. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`, but any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (it is a public export of @calcom/core) that reads `.calendar` now receives a promise and will silently misbehave (e.g. truthiness checks always pass, method calls throw). Additionally, these promises are created and left unhandled inside `flatMap`: if a credential's app module fails to load, the rejection has no handler attached, giving an unhandled rejection. Consider making `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolving the calendars (with per-item error handling) before returning.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate's review identifies the same underlying concern as the golden comment: when a credential's app module fails to load, the resulting rejection is unhandled, and it recommends per-item error handling before returning. Although the candidate also discusses a broader contract change, the core issue of gracefully handling import failures matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
try/catch around forEach(async ...) cannot catch anything and deletions are not awaited

Same defect as in the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { await getCalendar(...) ... })` returns immediately, so the enclosing `try/catch` that logs errors is dead code and any failure of `calendar.deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection. The reschedule email is sent and `true` returned before the external cancellations are known to have completed, which can leave orphaned calendar/video events. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` so the awaited work is covered by the try/catch.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core defect: forEach(async ...) is fire-and-forget, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch failures and calendar/video deletions are not awaited. It also recommends Promise.all with map, matching the golden comment's suggested fix.

false_positives.candidate:
import() calls are evaluated eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded

The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … directly, which means every dynamic import is *started* the moment `packages/app-store/index.ts` is evaluated. The resulting object holds already-pending/resolved module promises, so all ~28 app packages (and their transitive deps such as googleapis, @microsoft/..., stripe, etc.) are still pulled into the bundle and executed at startup; the only thing that changed is that the consumer now has to `await` them. To get the intended benefit the map must hold thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call sites must invoke them (`await appStore[key]()`). As written the PR adds async plumbing across the codebase without delivering the stated code-splitting/startup win.

try/catch around forEach(async ...) cannot catch anything and deletions are not awaited

Converting the `forEach` callback to `async` means `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` returns before any deletion happens, so the surrounding `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can never observe a failure — rejections escape as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged. The function also proceeds to send the reschedule email and `return true` while the external calendar/video cancellations may not have executed. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` inside the try block.
